research_rules: Browse Google/web search for every assigned institution. Read at least one institution-specific official page plus another relevant page or authoritative affiliating-university source where available. ICAR data alone is not enough for a full page.

Shiksha/Collegedunia may supply secondary facts, but independently confirm important fees, eligibility, admissions, accreditation and statistics with official sources. Record access failures; do not bypass a block.

Write original copy from factual notes. Do not lightly paraphrase, reproduce distinctive wording, lift reviews, testimonials or ranking claims. Respect per-source word limits across the entire content pack; spread researched copy across several primary pages, and keep source-derived prose concise.

Do not guess official domains, addresses, contact details, fees, exams, percentages, hostel availability, placement figures, current-open admissions or generic promises. Unknown scalar facts remain null; unavailable arrays remain empty and get verification gaps. Useful prose can explain the known situation without filler.
Date every volatile fact by its actual source year. 2025 fees or NIRF ranks are not 2026 values. ICAR intake in the register is historical accreditation scope, not a live admission seat count.

Agriculture-focused institution profiles, not a catalogue of every non-agricultural degree. Keep Khalsa veterinary and SRM horticulture scopes accurate. Each independent college remains a college profile even though the current app route says university.
Reuse the locally audited ICAR identity and validity as provenance, with its limitations. If new official evidence conflicts, record the conflict; do not silently alter the 58 membership.

Save progress incrementally in your own batch directory, one JSON per completed institution. Do not modify application source, other batches, the research audit or CMS records. Keep all work under D:/agrico-frontend.

About 450-750 useful original words per institution is a target, not permission to fill unavailable sections with invented facts or repetitive advice. Useful facts and specificity take precedence over length.
